picks.comment: The featured pick: Mark's stacked RB room carries the day, Mick's horseshoe finally falls out, and Mels-16 wins by 50.
picks.recap: Right winner, aggressive math. Mark won by 19.76, leaving the 50-point call 30.24 points short. Brock Purdy (28.48) and Jaylen Waddle (24.80) made the QB/WR2 doubts look pretty silly. Josh Allen still dropped 40.82, and Dalton Kincaid's 22.50 deserves an apology.

picks.comment: Two one-time champions face off. Chris pulls this one out behind a bounce-back game from Ja’Marr Chase. I think KC leans less on the run against Indy this week, giving Rashee Rice his chance to shine.
picks.recap: The Chase bounce-back call landed: 26.50 points after 3.20 in Week 1. Rice added 12.30, and Chris won by 39.92. Chalk one up for the Swami.

picks.comment: Another battle of champions. This time, the defending champ takes the L thanks to a lack of firepower at running back. Mark's team is a little too well balanced here. I'm taking Mark.
picks.recap: The defending champ took the L, just as called. Mark won by 26.54 behind DeVonta Smith (30.70), Christian McCaffrey (22.60), and Jake Ferguson (20.30). Daniel's starting RBs combined for 17.10.

picks.comment: With a question mark around Zay Flowers' availability and a pretty weak RB2 spot, I don't think Brett can sustain the firepower he showed in Week 1. Jason takes this one—even with Fairbairn finishing as his third-highest scorer this week.
picks.recap: Brett heard the doubt and responded with 152.98 points and a 40.78-point win. Goff (32.78), Gibbs (23.30), and Olave (22.60) kept the firepower coming. Even JSN's 45.50 couldn't save Gotham. Fairbairn finished fourth on Jason's team, not third.

picks.comment: Dillon is leaning a little too hard on an offense going up against Houston this week. Grim Reaper takes the W in what I'm calling the lowest-scoring matchup of the week.
picks.recap: The Commish picked himself and paid for it. Dillon won by 4.66 despite DJ Moore scoring minus 0.10. This wasn't the lowest-scoring matchup either: Nick and Chris combined for 184.12, below this game's 219.82. Grim Reaper is now named Silence of the Lamb on Yahoo.

picks.comment: This might be the closest matchup on paper. I'm taking the Dallas stack, but it'll take a big effort from Jonathan Taylor on Sunday night to push Slim Pickens past Dusty.
picks.recap: Right winner, wrong suspense level. Slim Pickens won by 59.08 and led the league with 156.36. Taylor delivered 29.20 and Dak added 29.76, but Davante Adams stole the show with 42.50. Dusty never got the close finish the Swami expected.

weeks.summary: Week 2: 4–2 (66.7%). The Swami nailed both Marks, Chris, and Slim Pickens. Brett blew up the Gotham pick, and picking the Commish over Dillon did not age well. The winners count; the extra trash talk gets its own report card below.

picks.comment: This isn't a matchup of the week based on firepower. It's quite the opposite. I legit opened this matchup for this write-up and said, ‘What the fuck am I looking at?’ The only good RB either team has is currently on one of the most inept offenses in the league. I legit think this one comes down to Trey McBride and the ghost of Puka Nacua vs. Amon-Ra St. Brown by himself. I actually think it might be fun if the two managers benched the rest of their teams. Who the fuck is Konata Mumpfield, and why the hell is he on a fantasy roster? Winner: West Coast, I guess?
picks.recap: The featured coin flip landed on the wrong coast. Daniel won by 14.48, with Michael Wilson's 25.90 leading the way and McBride adding 16.50. Puka stayed on the bench, and the final starting lineup did not include Mumpfield. Dusty's 89.88 left West Coast still looking for its first win.

picks.comment: Jason is one person who hasn't really been hurt by injuries too much. Luckily, his RB1 has been getting touches taken by an 83-year-old Alvin Kamara, and David Montgomery has shown why Detroit didn't mind getting rid of him. Drake London finally gets a QB this week with Penix, and the Dallas RB1/WR1 duo will carry Tylor to the promised land.
picks.recap: The London call landed: 31.40 points, plus 41.50 combined from Lamb and Javonte Williams. Tylor finally got his first win, by 11.04. Jason had the escape route on his bench: McLaurin over Bateman would have flipped the result.

picks.comment: Tyler Shough is a force right now, but if Adonai Mitchell can't start turning those targets into points, I don't know how Nick survives. Nico might be back this week, but I don't think that's enough to push him past Brett. Gibbs and Olave have been an insane combo so far. If Olave's big-ass helmet saves him from getting any more scrambled, Bretty is going to be tough to beat.
picks.recap: Brett was every bit as tough to beat as advertised. Gibbs (41.40), Wilson (29.70), Warren (23.60), and Olave (22.70) powered a 76.76-point win and the season's new high score. Shough's 24.80 was not nearly enough for Nick.

picks.comment: Jason's team is looking really nice right now. The RBs are in an okay spot, and surprisingly, Davante Adams has been able to dust off the old knees and bring himself into relevance again. I do think Chris has a shot here if Rashee can do something and Watson takes over more snaps with Jayden Reed out. Unfortunately, I really don't think it's going to be enough.
picks.recap: The Swami gave Chris a chance, then picked against him. Fannin (24.10), Chase (24.80), Watson (22.60), and Rice (15.80) delivered a 21.88-point win. Adams scored 23.70 for Jason, but the rest of the comeback never arrived.

picks.comment: Dillon is currently relying on two players from CLE. Yes, that stands for Cleveland Browns, not some fun slogan like ‘Clutch. Legendary. Successful.’ Good luck with that one, big guy. I think Bijan bounces back with someone a bit more competent at the helm, and I think Baltimore learns from last game that giving Derrick Henry fewer snaps is a bad, bad thing. Mark Melquist is already 2–0, and I don't think that streak ends this week.
picks.recap: The Bijan bounce-back call was on target: 38.30 points. Henry added 21.90 and Purdy 31.28 as Mark stayed unbeaten with a 21.38-point win. Dillon's 130.10 was respectable, but respectable does not beat 151.48.

picks.comment: I don't even want to write this one. I hate both owners almost equally, and I hope they both lose. Screw you guys. Burn in hell. All joking aside, I again think Josh Allen just isn't enough firepower—although he is a hell of a lot of firepower—and Mark's well-balanced team propels him to a win.
picks.recap: Mark won by 50.18 behind Bowers (30.60) and McCaffrey (21.60). Allen scored 19.46, but Overdue Bills managed only 68.26 overall. The balance-over-one-star pick paid off.

weeks.summary: Week 3: 4–2 (66.7%). The Swami nailed Tylor, Brett, Mels-16, and Mark's Team. Daniel and Chris spoiled the other two picks. Season record: 8–4 (66.7%), with Week 1 excluded.

weeks.editorialNote: Original previews and picks are preserved below. Final scores, starting lineups, and benches verified on Yahoo October 6, 2026; stat corrections may apply through October 8.

picks.comment: Brett just dropped 180.26, so naturally this is where I pick against him. Yahoo has DonkeyWoodDean favored by 11.78, and Gibbs gets a Carolina defense allowing the third-most fantasy points to running backs. That's a hell of a starting point. Slim counters with Trevor Lawrence, Jonathan Taylor, and Jeremiyah Love, while Pickens and Adams bring the receiving firepower. I like Love and Matthew Golden to help Slim steal this one, even if Brett's Goff-Gibbs-LaPorta stack makes Sunday night extremely uncomfortable. Brett gets the spotlight; Slim gets my pick.
picks.recap: Brett got the spotlight and the win. Flowers (28.80), Goff (23.48), Olave (22.60), LaPorta (22.40), and Reichard (20.00) helped DonkeyWoodDean cruise by 65.00. Flowers replaced Brian Thomas Jr. in the final flex spot. Taylor's 22.70 was Slim's only score above 20; the upset never materialized.

picks.comment: The Commish finally got a win, and his reward is Bijan, Henry, and Kyren. Very thoughtful of the schedule. Mels-16 also has Joe Burrow at quarterback now, while Silence of the Lamb is rolling with Sam Darnold. Lamb and London can keep me in it, but Mark's running back room is a weekly problem and Jadarian Price is carrying a questionable tag in my flex. Yahoo favors Mels by 17.41. I'm taking Mark and hoping those three backs at least have the decency to make it quick.
picks.recap: Right winner, wrong idea about making it quick. The Commish scored 165.42 behind Lamb's 44.30 and Javonte's 31.30, and still lost by 31.20. McMillan (48.20), Kyren (36.70), Bijan (30.70), and Burrow (28.72) pushed Mels-16 to 196.62, the new season high. Mark's running back room was every bit the problem advertised.

picks.comment: Nick needs a response after Brett turned last week's matchup into a crime scene. Nico Collins is back in Beast Infection's starting lineup, though he's questionable, and his 17.98 projection matters a lot next to Walker and Egbuka. Gotham has Lamar marked questionable too, plus JSN and Terry McLaurin actually in the lineup this time. Yahoo separates these teams by just 2.32 points. I'm taking Nick's Walker-Collins combination to get him over the line, but both owners need to watch those injury tags.
picks.recap: The Walker-Collins call landed: 67.70 combined, powering a 54.06-point win. Nick's final lineup used Antonio Williams at WR and Egbuka in the flex. Gotham started McLaurin for zero and Pitts instead of Andrews; Jameson Williams' 19.20 also stayed on the bench. None of those swaps alone would have erased the deficit.

picks.comment: Chris just beat Slim Pickens, and now Chase, Watson, and Rice get another chance to carry the offense. Swift and TreVeyon Henderson are the current running backs, so this pick is about the receivers doing the heavy lifting. Daniel can answer with McBride, Michael Wilson, and Jordan Addison, but Pollard's questionable tag adds another headache. Yahoo gives Chris a 12.49-point edge, and I'm with it. The defending champ gets my respect; Chris gets the pick.
picks.recap: The receivers did not do the heavy lifting. Chris managed 61.58 with Rice scoring zero and Chase adding just 5.70. Daniel's final lineup included Puka, who delivered 30.70, alongside Maye's 27.16. A 71.68-point loss is a pretty firm rebuttal to the Swami. Monangai's 31.00 and Tate's 24.50 sat on Chris's bench.

picks.comment: Mark can roll out Mahomes, McCaffrey, Jefferson, DeVonta, and Bowers, which makes picking against him feel irresponsible. Fortunately, responsibility has never been the Swami's strongest position. Cook and Chase Brown give Dillon a real puncher's chance, and Higgins gets Jacksonville alongside Brown. Yahoo favors Mark by 16.32, but Jefferson and DeVonta are questionable; Dillon has his own tags on DJ Moore and flex option Kenyon Sadiq. Give me Dillon's backs and a big Higgins day to pull the upset.
picks.recap: The Higgins call delivered 29.70, and Dillon's final lineup upgrades helped finish the job: Stroud scored 26.08 and Judkins 21.60. Mark started Sutton and Malik Washington with Jefferson and DeVonta out. Dillon won by 33.08; Yahoo's final projections had this nearly even, with Mark favored by just 0.07.

picks.comment: Yahoo has Dusty ahead by 8.29, but I'm trusting the Josh Allen shrine one more time. Allen and Kincaid get New England, and Mick needs Hubbard and Croskey-Merritt to give that Buffalo pair some help. West Coast is starting Barkley and a questionable Bucky Irving alongside Amon-Ra, Parker Washington, and Josh Downs. That's enough talent to punish this pick, especially with Jalen Coker also questionable for Mick. I'm taking Overdue Bills on an Allen-Kincaid afternoon that does the heavy lifting.
picks.recap: Right winner, different heroes. Hubbard's 28.90 and Doubs' 23.80 led Mick to a 40.14-point win. Allen added 19.52, but Kincaid managed only 1.70, so the Buffalo-pair prediction gets partial credit at best. Dusty's Barkley and Irving combined for 8.10, while Nabers' 26.20 and Deebo's 18.00 stayed on the bench.

weeks.summary: Week 4: 4–2 (66.7%). Mels-16, Beast Infection, Dillon, and Overdue Bills delivered. Brett steamrolled the featured upset pick, and Daniel dismantled Chris. Season record: 12–6 (66.7%), with Week 1 excluded.

weeks.editorialNote: Original Week 5 previews and picks are preserved. Final scores, starters, and benches checked on Yahoo October 13, 2026; corrections may apply through October 15.

picks.comment: The Commish is 1–3 despite scoring 537.60 points. Mark is 3–1, but Yahoo gives Silence a 9.07-point edge. Give me the Commish to turn those points into a damn win.
picks.recap: The Commish finally got a win to match the points. Likely's 32.40, London's 21.80, and Shrader's 21.30 helped Silence survive Lamb's 2.90 and beat Mark by 10.50. Bowers (26.00), Rodgers (22.00), and Jefferson (18.80) kept Mark close, but the supporting cast could not close the gap.

picks.comment: Nick just beat Gotham by 54.06, while Slim took a 65-point beating from Brett. Yahoo still favors Slim by 21.01. Beast is 2–2, Slim is 1–3, and I’m backing Nick to keep his momentum going. Beast Infection gets the spotlight and my upset pick.
picks.recap: The spotlight was on Nick. The points were on Jason's side. Pickens (31.00), Golden (23.30), Adams (22.10), and Braelon Allen (21.60) powered Slim to a 56.40-point win. Shough's 1.84 put Beast in a hole, and Walker was on a bye. Egbuka and Stevenson tried to help, but this upset call was dead well before the final tally.

picks.comment: Chris scored 61.58 last week. That’s not a repeat performance I’m betting on. Both teams are 2–2, but Yahoo favors Chris by 19.03. Give me Chris to bounce back and leave Mick staring at the scoreboard.
picks.recap: The bounce-back call survived, barely. Watson's 35.30 and Chase's 19.70 carried Chris to an 8.68-point win despite Bagent scoring 3.18. Allen dropped 34.50 for Mick, but the shrine needed more help from the receivers. Starting Bourne (12.00) instead of Concepcion (1.50) would have flipped the result to a 1.82-point Overdue Bills win.

picks.comment: Brett is 4–0 with a league-leading 660.56 points. Daniel just demolished Chris, but this is a bigger problem. Yahoo gives Brett a 14.54-point edge. Until someone stops this donkey, I’m riding with DonkeyWoodDean.
picks.recap: Until someone stops the donkey, keep riding. Gibbs (40.70) and Warren (39.80) combined for 80.50, with Goff (28.94) and Wilson (26.40) adding to the damage. Brett's 206.74 is the new season high, and he won by 70.58. Puka matched Gibbs with 40.70 for Daniel, but one monster game could not keep up with the whole damn stable.

picks.comment: Dillon just knocked off Mark by 33.08. Dusty is 0–4 and still hunting that first win. Yahoo separates them by only 2.10 points. I’m taking Dillon and making West Coast wait another week.
picks.recap: West Coast finally showed up, and Dillon got the bill. Irving (34.50), Washington (33.40), Nabers (32.10), and Love (28.28) powered Dusty's 176.68 and a 52.62-point first win. Daniels (35.26), Evans (29.30), and Cook (25.80) gave Dillon a solid total, but this was the week the basement fought back.

picks.comment: Mels is 4–0 and just dropped 196.62. Gotham is 1–3 with three straight losses. Yahoo favors Mark by 24.12, which makes this pick look ridiculous on paper. Good. Give me Gotham to spoil the perfect record.
picks.recap: The ridiculous upset pick stayed ridiculous. Mels won by 16.34 behind Burrow (24.60), Henry (24.00), and Tyler Warren (21.40), keeping the perfect record intact. JSN's 25.80 helped Gotham, but Montgomery's 1.10 did not. Woody Marks over Montgomery alone would not have won it; combine that with Pitts over Andrews and Gotham could have flipped the result.

weeks.summary: Week 5: 3–3 (50.0%). Silence of the Lamb, Chris, and Brett delivered. Slim and Mels spoiled the upset calls, and West Coast finally got its first win. Season record: 15–9 (62.5%), with Week 1 excluded.

weeks.editorialNote: Original Week 6 picks and previews are preserved. Final scores, original projections, starters, and benches checked on Yahoo October 20, 2026; corrections may apply through October 22.

picks.comment: Daniel can make this uncomfortable, but I like Nick’s path to a bounce-back. Walker gives Beast a strong foundation, and Collins and Egbuka bring the kind of receiving upside that can swing a matchup. Daniel has plenty of punch with Puka and McBride; I’m backing Nick to get more help across the lineup. Beast Infection gets the spotlight and the win.
picks.recap: The bounce-back call landed. Walker's 30.90 and Shough's 26.96 gave Nick the foundation, while Egbuka added 17.80 in an 11.06-point win. Johnson scored zero and Brown managed 5.70, so this was not exactly comfortable. Daniel got 23.80 from Maye and 20.30 from Metcalf, but Folk's 1.00 and a quieter day from Puka left him short. Beast won as Yahoo's final 7.35-point underdog.

picks.comment: Dusty finally reminded everyone his team can put up a fight. Unfortunately, I still like the Lamb and London combination to give the Commish the edge. West Coast can absolutely make me regret this, but I’m trusting my playmakers to finish the job. Give me Silence of the Lamb.
picks.recap: The Commish turned another pick into a win, by 21.88. Likely (23.90) and Cousins (22.52) led the scoring; Lamb and London combined for 28.20. Nabers gave Dusty 31.50, but Irving and Lloyd combined for only 7.90. Tucker's 26.70 stayed on Tylor's bench, so there was still room for the victory to be more comfortable.

picks.comment: Chris has the receivers to turn this into a headache, but I like Dillon’s running backs to keep his lineup moving. Cook and the rest of that backfield give him a way to stay in it without waiting for a receiver to save the afternoon. I’m taking Dillon to grind this one out.
picks.recap: Chris made the Swami pay for picking against him. Swift (23.00), Caleb Williams (19.50), Tate (19.00), and Flournoy (17.00) delivered an 8.50-point win. Cook and Daniels combined for 48.30 for Dillon, but zeroes from Judkins and DJ Moore left too much to overcome. Even Dillon's best possible lineup from this roster would have finished short.

picks.comment: Josh Allen can drag Mick into just about any matchup, so this is no free ride for Brett. I’m leaning on Wilson and Olave to give DonkeyWoodDean enough receiving firepower to get through a tougher week. Mick has a real opening here, but I still trust Brett’s receivers to make the difference. I’m staying on the damn donkey.
picks.recap: The donkey finally stopped, and Mick was the one holding the rope. Hubbard (22.10), Bass (18.70), and Allen (18.30) helped Overdue Bills win by 49.42 and post the week's highest score, 125.50. Brett's final lineup left Olave's 14.30 on the bench while Brian Thomas Jr. scored zero. That swap alone would not have saved the unbeaten record.

picks.comment: JSN already played and got rolling, giving Gotham a strong start. I still like Slim’s mix of Taylor in the backfield and Pickens and Adams through the air. There are more ways for that group to carry the afternoon, and I’m trusting Slim to find one.
picks.recap: Slim found the answer to Gotham's early JSN surge. Golden scored 25.40, Taylor added 21.10, and the Chiefs defense supplied 15.00 in a 14.84-point win. JSN (28.40) and Tuten (24.70) gave Gotham a chance, but Andrews' 1.40 hurt. Pitts scored 23.00 on the bench; that one swap would have turned this into a 6.76-point Gotham win.

picks.comment: Mark’s Team has the star power to make picking against him feel stupid. I’m doing it anyway. Bijan, Henry, and Kyren give Mels a backfield I hate betting against, and the rest of the lineup doesn’t need to be spectacular when those guys get going. Give me Mels to wear him down.
picks.recap: The backfield the Swami hated betting against combined for just 22.00 from Bijan, Henry, and Kyren. McCaffrey scored 30.70 by himself for Mark's Team, with DeVonta adding 20.50. Mark won by 22.02 despite Skattebo scoring zero. Mels' perfect record ended, and the Swami's confidence in that running back room got a fairly direct response.

weeks.summary: Week 6: 3–3 (50.0%). Beast Infection, Silence of the Lamb, and Slim Pickens delivered. Chris beat the Dillon pick, while Overdue Bills and Mark’s Team ended both unbeaten runs. Season record: 18–12 (60.0%), with Week 1 excluded.
